name: PeopleFinders

steps.note: This address opens a choice, not a form. A Right to Opt-out card with a Next button sits at the top; below an OR rule is a Free Identity Monitoring offer with its own Learn More button, and nothing here ever touches that. Further down the same page is a Record Suppression Form, and that one is a trap: see notes.

The door. It replaces the choice card with the short form the rest of these steps fill. Nothing has been sent at this point. The Learn More button below the OR rule carries the same css class, so the visible label is what tells them apart, and a run that cannot find Next by its text stops rather than pressing the other one.
The boxes on this short form carry no labels beside them; the words inside them are their labels. None of the four is marked required on the page.
The page says the link to the removal form is sent to this address, so it has to be an inbox the person can open.

choices: An agent authorized to act on behalf of the subject of the request
steps.note: A dropdown reading The subject of the request on the capture, whose two answers were read from that page's own markup on verified_on. It carries no agent_value_literal. The page's own note says an authorized agent's address receives the link and that confirmation then goes to both addresses, so the agent answer may need nothing extra, but nobody has selected it and captured what follows, and who is asking is not a thing to find out by trying it on a live form.

steps.prompt: PeopleFinders puts a reCAPTCHA under this form. Tick it yourself, then say when it is done.
steps.note: Handed over, never worked around. Nothing here solves it.

steps.prompt: The name and email are filled in. One box is still unticked, and it reads: I authorize PeopleFinders to send communications relating to my privacy request to the email address(es) provided, and it certifies that you are the subject of the request or an agent authorized to act for them. Check the values, then say yes and I will tick that box and send the request.
steps.note: Combined with the captcha gate before it, because the token this page issues can expire while the values are being read.

selector.label: I authorize PeopleFinders to send communications relating to my privacy request to the email address(es) provided.

steps.note: Ticked only after the gate above, because the certification is the person's to make.

steps.prompt: PeopleFinders is sending a link to that address, and the form behind it is the one that actually removes the record. Open it yourself and fill it in: it arrives with the name and email already filled and asks for a phone number, a date of birth, a street address, a city, and a state. Two things to know before you open it. The link works once, so open it when you have a few minutes rather than to see what it looks like; opening it a second time expires it and you have to ask for a new one. And the page says a link left more than 24 hours has to be requested again. The State/Region box on that form looks like a plain text box and is really a dropdown, so pick from the list rather than typing. When you reach the confirmation page, tell me what it said.
steps.note: This is where the manifest stops and the broker's flow does not. Nothing has been removed at this point; a link has been asked for. The form behind the link is not automated and will not be: its address is single-use and carries the key in the URL. What it asks for is recorded here from the runs of 2026-09-10 rather than from a capture in this repository, and it is described as what a person was asked rather than as what a page says.

verification.success_when: PeopleFinders' own search no longer returns a record for this name and city. The page is blunt that this is not permanent: it says the data is not removed from its original source, that it may still appear on other websites, and that new public records arrive regularly so the information may appear again, which is why it recommends refreshing the request periodically.

additional_captures.of: The short form behind the Next button, on the same visit, with every box empty. It carries the four directions this flow is written from, the 24-hour condition on the emailed link, and the 3 days this manifest's recheck window comes from

The Record Suppression Form at the bottom of the same page, on the same visit, with every box empty. Committed as evidence for a negative: it is the form six submissions failed against and the one no step here touches

id_requirements.note: No account, payment, notarised document, or photo ID appears on either form. The choice page states in its own words that both routes it offers are free and that no trial or payment is required.

notes: Written from three frames captured on verified_on, all reachable without sending anything. The route changed and the old manifest was filling the wrong form, which is worth stating plainly because the failure was silent. There are two forms on /opt-out. The Record Suppression Form at the bottom of the page is the form the emailed link opens, rendered without the one-time key that link carries, so submitting it directly can never succeed: it returns the site's own server error and greys out its Submit button. Six submissions across two days failed that way, two of them typed by hand, and it read as an outage rather than a closed door. It was not an outage. Do not fill the lower form. The working route is the Next button at the top and it is the only one this manifest uses. The flow the page states in four numbered directions: name and email and a captcha here, a link by email, the removal form behind that link, then a confirmation page and a confirmation email, with 3 days to removal. That last figure is where recheck_after_days comes from and it is on the capture. The link is single-use; opening it a second time expires it and a new one has to be requested, which was learned by doing it rather than from any page, and the page separately says a link left more than 24 hours needs requesting again. One detail from the lower form's own markup, recorded because it will bite whoever automates the emailed form later: State/Region is a select with 55 options carrying a class called text-input, so it renders like a plain box and a run that types into it is typing into a dropdown. What the captures show and what they do not: the choice card and its Next button, the monitoring offer nothing touches, every box and label on the short form, the authorize sentence, the reCAPTCHA, the Send Request button, and the four directions are all on the frames; the css fallback on the Next step and the dropdown's two answers were read from the page's markup on the same visit, and no image holds a browser address bar, so home_url, source_url, and optout_url record addresses that were open rather than anything legible on them. Two things were done to the pages before they were captured, and neither adds or removes anything the broker wrote: the cookie banner was hidden on two frames, and each page was viewed zoomed out so its section fits one frame. One box on the lower form had been filled by the browser's own autofill before anybody typed. It was cleared before the shutter, and it is the reason a run reads a field back after writing it rather than trusting that an empty box was empty. The emailed form itself, the email-sent page, the expired-link page and the confirmation page are not in this repository. They exist only inside a real run, and the versions in the maintainer's draft folder were painted by another tool and have not been checked by this project's reviewer. A note is not a commit.
